about: Second batch from the full read of the older packs, 2026-11-12: five more near-twin categories and four single clues that repeated a fact in their own round.

rewrites.name: SHOVEL READY
rows: A Bedouin shepherd's stone, tossed into a cave near Qumran in 1947, led to these ancient manuscripts
In 1940 four teenagers stumbled on Ice Age paintings of bulls and horses in this French cave
Hikers in the Alps in 1991 came upon this 5,300-year-old mummy, tattoos, copper axe and all
Leonard Woolley's digs of the 1920s at this Sumerian city in Iraq uncovered royal tombs heaped with gold
After digging up the labyrinthine palace at Knossos, Arthur Evans named this Cretan culture for a mythic king

rewrites.name: BUBBLE TROUBLE
rows: At the height of a 1630s Dutch mania, a single bulb of this flower could trade for more than a house
Risky 'subprime' mortgages went bad in 2007 and 2008, bursting the bubble in this market and shaking banks worldwide
In the 1920s speculators snapped up swampy lots in this state, a land boom that a 1926 hurricane helped flatten
In the 1840s Britons poured their savings into shares of hundreds of new lines for this kind of transport, a 'Mania' that ruined thousands
Japan's 'bubble economy' peaked in December 1989, when this Tokyo stock index came within a whisker of 39,000

rewrites.name: THE PHILANTHROPIST'S STONE
rows: This Microsoft co-founder started a foundation in 2000 that grew into the world's biggest private charity, fighting malaria and polio
In 2006 this 'Oracle of Omaha' pledged most of his fortune to charity, and he later co-founded the Giving Pledge
This Kodak founder gave away most of his fortune, including millions sent to MIT under the alias 'Mr. Smith'
Called America's first self-made female millionaire, this hair-care mogul bankrolled anti-lynching efforts
This Sears, Roebuck president teamed up with Booker T. Washington to help build some 5,000 schools for Black children in the rural South

rewrites.name: FOUR-LEGGED FILM STARS
rows: This scruffy little mutt rescues two kidnapped children in a 1974 family film that carries his name
This polite little pig learns to herd sheep in a 1995 barnyard film
A slobbery St. Bernard named for this composer turns the Newton family's house upside down in a 1992 comedy
This wire fox terrier sniffed out clues for Nick and Nora Charles in the 'Thin Man' movies
This talking Army mule starred in a series of 1950s comedies with Donald O'Connor

rewrites.name: THE MOTOWN SOUND
rows: Young Michael sang lead for this brother act from Gary, Indiana, on 'ABC' and 'I Want You Back'
'Baby I Need Your Loving' and 'I Can't Help Myself (Sugar Pie, Honey Bunch)' were smashes for this Motown quartet
This Miracles frontman sang 'The Tracks of My Tears' and wrote 'My Guy'
'Please Mr. Postman' gave Motown its first No. 1 pop hit in 1961, sung by this girl group
With an $800 family loan, this former boxer built Motown Records in Detroit

singles.name: DEEP SKY DIVING
singles.clue: Our solar system sits in a spiral arm of this galaxy, seen from Earth as a pale band across a dark night sky
singles.why: Andromeda repeated FAR OUT #1 in the same round.

singles.name: A TAXING SITUATION
singles.clue: 'No taxation without' this, cried colonists angry at duties passed by a Parliament in which they had no seats
singles.why: The Boston Tea Party repeated UP IN ARMS #1 in the same round.

singles.name: A TAXING SITUATION
singles.clue: In 1765 Parliament taxed the colonists' newspapers, legal papers and even playing cards with this measure, repealed within a year
singles.why: The Whiskey Rebellion repeated UP IN ARMS #2 in the same round.

singles.name: DECIPHER ME THIS
singles.clue: Carved on Viking memorial stones, the angular letters of the futhark alphabet go by this name, also a word for any mysterious sign
singles.why: The hieroglyphs clue told the same fact as THE WRITE STUFF #1 in the same round.
